investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T10:55–11:03Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning and causing the eval to time out without producing any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning and causing the eval to time out without producing any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were available and unused at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a misconfigured resource request or quota policy would need investigation.

If the remote-agent-state eval passes on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.
If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create passed in the same run window, the root cause would be localized to the state-polling logic rather than shared VM scheduling capacity.

If the pod's node affinity selector was recently changed to exclude more nodes (reducing the eligible pool below 2), the primary cause would be a misconfigured affinity rule rather than VM slot exhaustion.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node plugin or resource registration rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on affinity-eligible nodes and fails fast with a capacity signal before attempting pod creation.

Add a node-affinity-pool eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2 with available VM slots), catching pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Add a preemption-eligibility eval that verifies at least one preemption victim exists on affinity-eligible nodes, so zero-preemption conditions are surfaced as a distinct warning before they block scheduling.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to record the pod scheduling latency as evidence (e.g., schedulingLatencyMs), enabling trend detection of degrading VM slot availability before full exhaustion occurs.

Add a cross-check eval that correlates remote-agent-create success with remote-agent-state readiness, so a create-succeeds-but-state-never-ready pattern can be distinguished from a create-fails pattern.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). Because pod scheduling is a prerequisite for agent creation, the eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918 (createAgent call) never returned a live agent, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the message assertion ("hello from aura") unverifiable. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 147s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=152264, endedAt=2026-07-15T11:03:07.910Z — the check ran for ~152 seconds, consistent with the scheduler timeout described in the message.
failed-check.evidence: raw evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, confirming the agent pod never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, matching the empty evidence object.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck for 121s, latencyMs=124408, endedAt=2026-07-15T10:58:04.234Z — the resource exhaustion predates the runtime check by ~5 minutes.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message to remote-agent-runtime, latencyMs=151412, endedAt=2026-07-15T11:00:35.646Z — all three checks in the remote-agents feature share the same failure mode.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — this call requires a schedulable pod; if the pod cannot be scheduled, no agent identity or runtime response is ever produced.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract at lines 266-270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a running agent pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all concurrent or recently created remote-agent VMs have consumed the full VM slot allocation on the 2 kata/peerpods nodes, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported by the identical scheduler message across all three sibling checks spanning a ~5-minute window (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata/peerpods nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were removed, cordoned, or had their labels changed, all 6 nodes would be ineligible. The 4-node mismatch is consistent with a static affinity rule rather than a transient condition.

Tertiary — VM slot quota set too low for the current eval concurrency: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node may be configured at a value that is too small to absorb simultaneous eval runs plus any live user workloads sharing the same pool. No user-traffic evidence is present to confirm live workload contention, so this remains a hypothesis.

Lower confidence — a prior eval run's cleanup did not release VM slots: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete a previous agent, its VM slot would remain consumed. The sibling remote-agent-create failure at 10:58 UTC (before the runtime check at 11:00 UTC) is consistent with slots being held from an earlier run, but no cleanup-failure evidence is present in the packet.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool capacity: run kubectl describe on the two eligible nodes to determine how many VM slots are allocated vs. available. If all slots are consumed, identify and terminate any leaked or idle remote-agent pods.

Audit the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it reliably deletes remote-agent pods after each eval run. If cleanup is not guaranteed on failure paths, leaked pods will hold VM slots and cause recurring scheduling failures.

Determine whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot limit per node is sufficient for the expected eval concurrency plus any live workloads sharing the pool. If not, coordinate with the infrastructure team to increase the slot allocation or add additional kata/peerpods nodes.

Verify the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods: confirm that the 4 non-kata nodes are intentionally excluded and that the 2 kata nodes are healthy, schedulable, and not cordoned.

Re-run all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) after any capacity remediation to confirm the eval passes and all required evidence fields are populated.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe on the two kata/peerpods nodes showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime eval immediately after this failure, with no cluster changes, would suggest a transient scheduler condition rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod was scheduled but the agent process itself failed (e.g., a pod in Running or Error state with application-level logs) would shift the root cause from scheduling to agent runtime.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state while remote-agent-runtime fails would indicate the failure is isolated to the runtime check rather than shared VM slot exhaustion.

Cluster event logs showing the 2 kata/peerpods nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reduced around 2026-07-15T10:55Z would confirm a node-level change rather than workload-driven exhaustion.
